query: How do you rebuild trust after it breaks?
why_in_two_sentences: Healthline is a strong two-sided guide (betrayed and betrayer) with a timeline and affair-specific advice; Crisis Text Line is thin and mostly a funnel to its hotline. Ours matches the two-track structure and goes further (the checking loop, structure over willpower, telling the present person from the original one), but Healthline covers one concrete dilemma we skip.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Two-track frame: the breaker supplies specific repeatable evidence, the hurt person learns to tell the present person from the original one
Explains why the checking keeps coming back even when it finds nothing
Sets the standard as transparency offered before it is asked for, plus tolerance of being checked

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer lays out both tracks and the honest six-months-to-two-years range, then recognition sentences; the searcher knows the real shape of the task immediately.
above_the_fold.theirs: Healthline opens by listing non-infidelity trust breaches (broken promises, withholding, not showing up in a crisis), broadening the reader's definition before any advice.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Should I ask for all the details of the affair, or is it better not to know?
What would it take for me to feel safe with this person again?
trust_signals: Healthline shows a named writer and PhD medical reviewer; Crisis Text Line leans on its crisis-service brand; ours has no byline, reviewer, or citations.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add guidance on the details question (how much disclosure about the betrayal helps versus harms); it is the one concrete dilemma Healthline covers that our affair FAQs skip.
